get.summary:
The actor's account's public access block, as S3 Control's
GetPublicAccessBlock gets it: `null` if it has none.

put.summary:
Sets the actor's account's public access block, which every one of its
buckets gets too, as S3 Control's PutPublicAccessBlock does.

delete.summary:
Removes the actor's account's public access block: only its buckets'
own apply.

post.summary:
Makes the account's root a one-time link to the console (24 hours): its
first, or one to recover the account, if the root lost its passkeys. It
replaces the root's last.

put.summary: Sets a bucket's CORS configuration, checked as PutBucketCors checks it.

delete.summary: Removes a bucket's CORS configuration: no other site's page may use it.

get.summary:
An object's data, as a file to save. It's always sent as an attachment of
no particular type, so that a browser never renders it as part of the UI.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The version to download; the current one if not given.

get.summary:
A bucket's lifecycle rules, as S3's GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration
gives them, but in the form they're stored in.

put.summary:
Replaces a bucket's lifecycle rules, as S3's
PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration does, which starts a new sweep of them.
Rules without an ID get one.

delete.summary:
Removes a bucket's lifecycle rules, as S3's DeleteBucketLifecycle does:
nothing expires from then on.

put.summary:
Writes an object from the request's body, as PutObject does (with the
bucket's default encryption, and as the user for SSE-KMS); its
`Content-Type` is the object's. At most 5 GiB, as a single PutObject.

delete.summary: Deletes a key, or one of its versions, as DeleteObject does.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description:
The version to remove for good; without it, the key is deleted as
DeleteObject does (a delete marker, in a versioned bucket).

put.summary:
Replaces a version's tags, as PutObjectTagging does (or, with none,
DeleteObjectTagging).

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The version whose tags to set; the current one if not given.

parameters.name: deleted
parameters.description: Also list keys whose current version is a delete marker.

put.summary:
Sets a bucket's policy, as PutBucketPolicy does: checked as S3 checks
it, and refused if it's public while public policies are blocked.
Sets a bucket's public access block, as PutPublicAccessBlock does.

delete.summary: Removes a bucket's public access block: only its account's applies.

put.summary:
Replaces a bucket's tags, as PutBucketTagging does (or, with none,
DeleteBucketTagging).

post.summary:
Starts a multipart upload, as CreateMultipartUpload does: for a file
larger than one upload may be (5 GiB), in parts.

delete.summary: Aborts a multipart upload, as AbortMultipartUpload does: its parts go.

post.summary:
Completes a multipart upload with its parts, in order, as
CompleteMultipartUpload does: the object is written then.

put.summary:
Uploads one part (1 to 10000) of a multipart upload, from the request's
body: at least 5 MiB but for the last, at most 5 GiB.
Enables or suspends a bucket's versioning, as PutBucketVersioning does.

get.summary: The nodes, each with the metrics it reports, if it's live.

post.summary:
Makes a new login, with a first passkey, for an enrollment link's
identity (using the link up), and signs in with it.

200.description: Signed in; the session's cookie is set

post.summary:
Adds an enrollment link's identity to the signed-in login (using the
link up).

Logs in to the KMS as each role without an identity there yet, from this
node, now rather than at its next maintenance pass. Fails with what went
wrong.

204.description: Every role has its identity in the KMS

get.summary:
How lifecycle sweeps are going: the rate, how long a round takes at it,
and each bucket's sweep.

post.summary: Signs in with a passkey, as the login's identity.

200.description: Signed in; the session's cookie is set

204.description: Signed out; the cookie is cleared

post.summary:
Keeps a node that's being removed, or was, as `cairn node keep` does: it
gets shards again; those that moved stay where they are.

Starts removing a node, as `cairn node remove` does: it gets no new
shards, and its shards move to the other nodes (see `mover`).

put.summary: Sets an OIDC provider, after checking its discovery document and keys.

delete.summary: Removes an OIDC provider: the identities at it no longer sign anyone in.

get.summary:
Where providers send the browser back to (register it with them): ends
the sign-in, and goes on to the console.

303.description: On to the console, signed in (or to the sign-in page, with what went wrong)

get.summary: The OIDC providers people may sign in at (for the sign-in page).

delete.summary:
Unlinks the signed-in login's identity at a provider (not its last way
in).

post.summary: Starts a sign-in at a provider.
Adds a passkey to the signed-in login.

put.summary: Renames one of the signed-in login's passkeys.

delete.summary:
Removes one of the signed-in login's passkeys (not its last), and ends
the sessions signed in with it.

put.summary: Makes one of a managed policy's versions its default (a rollback, say).
Sets a managed policy's tags, as IAM's TagPolicy and UntagPolicy would.

get.summary: A managed policy's versions (up to five), newest first.

delete.summary: Deletes one of a managed policy's versions, but its default.

patch.summary:
Renames or moves a user, as IAM's UpdateUser: allowed on it, and on
where it goes (its new ARN; moved only, its new path: see `iam`).

put.summary: Makes a role an admin, or not.

post.summary: Attaches a managed policy to a user.

delete.summary: Detaches a managed policy from a user.

put.summary:
Sets a user's permissions boundary, as IAM's
PutUserPermissionsBoundary (decided by the boundary asked for).

post.summary: Makes a role an enrollment link for the console, replacing its last.

Makes a new access key for a role, with a random ID and secret; a role
has at most two.

put.summary: Lets one of the role's access keys sign requests, or stops it.

delete.summary: Deletes one of the role's access keys.

get.summary: One of the role's inline policies, as it was set.

put.summary: Sets one of the role's inline policies, if it's a valid identity policy.

delete.summary: Deletes one of the role's inline policies.

put.summary: Sets a user's tags, as IAM's TagUser and UntagUser would.

Sets one of the redundancy settings (`data-shards`, `parity-shards`,
`repair-after`) for the whole cluster, as `cairn config set` does. The
node answering goes by it right away, the others within a heartbeat.

user_handle.description: The login the passkey is of, as the authenticator says.

compact.description: Blobs with enough garbage to be compacted.

consolidate.description: Blobs small enough to be consolidated.

convert.description:
Blobs large enough to be coded that aren't in the cluster's layout,
which the packer converts (see `packer::Layouts`).

copies.description:
Replicated blobs with more or fewer copies than the `parity-shards`
setting says (none while it isn't set), and how many copies the
mover is to add and to drop (see `mover`).

garbage_log.description:
Entries of the garbage log the packer hasn't folded yet: one per blob
that a statement deleted parts from.

moves.description:
Shards to move off nodes being removed, or down for longer than the
`repair-after` setting (see `mover`); and that setting, in minutes (0:
off).

packing.description: Blobs leased by packing jobs, right now.

garbage_bytes.description: Bytes of packed blobs that no part references anymore.

Block.description: A public access block's four flags.

arn.description: A managed policy's ARN: the account's own, or one of Cairn's.

BucketAccess.description:
Who may get at a bucket, besides its users' grants and policies: its
policy, and its public access block (see `s3::buckets::public_access`).

oneOf.description:
Its account's public access block, if it has one, which applies to
the bucket as well.

policy.description: Its policy, as GetBucketPolicy shows it; `null` if it has none.

public.description: Whether the policy makes the bucket public.

oneOf.description: Its public access block; `null` if it has none.

users.description:
The bucket's account's users whose own policies (inline and
attached) give them access to the whole bucket, and what.

BucketLifecycle.description: A bucket's lifecycle rules, if it has any.

oneOf.description:
Its account's public access block, if it has one, which applies to
the bucket as well.

default_kms_key.description:
The KMS key of its default encryption (SSE-KMS), if it has one: what a
write that asks for no encryption of its own is encrypted with.

object_lock.description: Whether it has Object Lock enabled (see `s3::object_lock`).

objects.description: Current versions that aren't delete markers.

public.description: Whether its policy makes it public (GetBucketPolicyStatus).

oneOf.description: Its public access block, if it has one.

roles.description:
The account's users whose policies give them access to the whole
bucket (see `who_has_access`).

Ceremony.description:
A ceremony's options, for `navigator.credentials` (WebAuthn's JSON form:
`PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON` or `…RequestOptionsJSON`), and
the ID of its challenge, to send back with the response.

state.description:
`active`, `removing` (its shards are moving to other nodes, see
`mover`) or `removed`.

oneOf.description: What the node reported, if it's live and answered.

stats_error.description: Why a live node's stats are missing.

ConsoleAccess.description: How a user signs in to the console (see `store::ConsoleAccess`).

enrolled.description: Whether it enrolled (a login is linked to it).

link_pending.description: Whether an enrollment link for it is out, and works still.

providers.description: The OIDC providers (their labels) it signs in at.

Counts.description: Counts of requests, by how they ended, and of what they moved.

client_errors.description: Answered with a 4xx: the client's fault (including denied requests).

latency_us.description: The sum of the times until the response's head was ready.

server_errors.description: Answered with a 5xx: a fault, or too few nodes.

Coverage.description: How much of the data the scrubber has checked (see `scrub`).

legacy_blobs.description: Committed blobs from before checksums, which can't be checked.

nodes.description:
What each node holds of checksummed data, and how recently it was
checked.

EncryptionInfo.description: How an object version is encrypted (see `s3::sse`).

kind.description:
`SSE-C` (with its client's key, which Cairn doesn't have), `SSE-KMS`
or `SSE-S3` (with Cairn's own key from the KMS).

kms_context.description: SSE-KMS: the encryption context its client gave, as JSON.

kms_key_id.description: SSE-KMS and SSE-S3: the name of the KMS key.

kms_key_version.description: SSE-KMS and SSE-S3: the version of the KMS key its data key is from.

EnrollCeremony.description:
What an enrollment link is for, and the options to make a new login's
passkey for it (signed out; signed in, `/enroll/link` adds it to the
login instead).

token.description: The token of the enrollment link (after its `#`).

EnrollmentLink.description:
A one-time link for a role to register its first passkey for the
console, valid 24 hours.

path.description: The link's path, for the console's URL.

url.description: The link, if this node serves the console (and so knows its URL).

oneOf.description: A "directory": the keys whose names continue past the prefix with `/`.

lost.description: Whether some of its bytes are intact on no replica (see `scrub`).

error.description: What went wrong, for a person to read.

bad_blocks.description: How many blocks failed; none if the whole file is at fault.

outcome.description:
`repaired`, `lost` (intact on no replica; still open), or `gone` (the
blob was deleted); none while open.

problem.description:
`missing`, `damaged`, or `catalog` (every block intact, but not the
file's CRC).

GcTotals.description: What garbage collection deleted since the node started.

admin.description:
Whether the user has `AdministratorAccess` (a root may do anything in
its account anyway).

arn.description: The identity's ARN, which policies name it by.

user.description: The user's name; `null`: the account's root.

Integrity.description:
What the scrubber found (see `scrub`): damaged and missing copies, and the
objects with data that's intact on no replica.

findings.description:
The open findings, then those resolved in the last 30 days, newest
first, up to 200.

lost.description:
The object versions (and uploads' parts) with lost bytes, the most
recently lost first, up to 500.

lost_objects.description: How many there are, all told.

recent.description:
Findings of the last day, by node: many of them in a short time are a
sign of a failing disk.

KmsLogin.description: A login to the KMS as a role.

at.description: When, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

error.description: Why it failed, if it did: what's likely wrong with the KMS's setup.

role.description: The role's ID, or `cairn` for Cairn itself (for SSE-S3).

KmsStatus.description: A node's KMS, as it sees it.

auth_mount.description:
Where the KMS's JWT auth method for Cairn is mounted (under `auth/`),
and the role of it that Cairn's logins use.

cairn_entity.description:
Cairn's own identity (entity) in the KMS, which is to be granted that
key, once the node has logged in as itself.

oneOf.description: The node's last login as a role, if it made one since it started.

last_success.description: When its last login that worked was, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

public_key.description:
The public key of the key the node signs its logins with (PEM): what
that auth method is to trust (`jwt_validation_pubkeys`). The same on
every node.

reachable.description: Whether the node could reach the KMS just now, and how it is.

sse_s3_key.description: SSE-S3's key, if Cairn has one: it uses it as itself.

LastSweep.description:
A bucket's last whole sweep, as `lifecycle_sweeps.last` keeps it. Times
are seconds since the Unix epoch.

last_step.description: When the last step began, and whether one is running now.

rate.description:
Object versions sweeps may read per hour, across the cluster; 0 if
they're paused.

reached_rate.description:
The rate steps have actually reached when they had more to do than
their share (an average over about the last hour), if they have.
Below `rate` if a step at a time can't go faster.

round_partial.description:
Whether some bucket has had no whole sweep yet, so that a round reads
more than `round_versions`.

round_secs.description:
How long a round takes at the rate reached, or set if it's lower (or
none was measured yet), in seconds; none if paused. Over a day, sweeps
fall behind, and expirations come that much later.

round_versions.description:
Versions a round of every bucket's sweep reads: the last whole sweep
of each, or what its first has read so far.

LifecycleBucket.description: A bucket's rules, and its sweep of them.

due.description:
When it gets its next turn: its next sweep, or, during one, its next
step (it's due if that's past).

rules.description: How many rules it has, and how many of them are enabled.

LifecycleDay.description: A day, UTC, as the number of days since 1970-01-01.

LifecycleFilter.description:
Which objects a rule applies to: those with keys starting with `prefix`,
sizes strictly between the bounds, and each of `tags` (with that value;
other tags don't matter). All of them, by default. A delete marker has no
size, and no tags: a filter on tags never matches one.

LifecycleFilterTag.description: A tag a filter asks for (see `s3::tags`).

newer_versions.description: How many of the newest noncurrent versions are kept regardless.

enabled.description: `Status`: a disabled rule is kept, but does nothing.

id.description: Its name, unique among the bucket's rules; one is made up if empty.

Listing.description: A page of a bucket's keys, rolled up at `/` like a directory listing.

next.description: What to pass as `after` for the next page, if there is one.

lost_bytes.description: How many of its stored bytes are lost.

since.description: When the first of them was found lost.

version_id.description: The version; none for a part of an upload in progress.

events.description: The most recent things a pass did or failed at, oldest first.

last_duration.description: How many seconds the last pass took.

running_since.description: When the pass that's running started.

sweep_shard.description:
Where the GC's file sweep is, of `shards` (blob directories; the
names are the console's).

Me.description: The signed-in login: who it acts as now, its identities, its passkeys.

cluster.description:
Whether it may see the cluster (`cairn:GetCluster`): it's an
operator, and the console shows it the cluster's pages.

mfa.description:
Whether it was signed in with a passkey (`aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent`;
else at an OIDC provider).

oidc.description: Its identities at OIDC providers, which sign it in too.

signed_in_at.description: The OIDC provider this session was signed in at, if it was.

MetricsReport.description: A node's metrics. Times are seconds since the Unix epoch.

in_flight.description: Requests whose response hasn't been sent in full yet.

object_lock.description:
Whether it has Object Lock enabled (and so is versioned) from the
start: it can't be disabled again.

NewKey.description: A new access key, whose secret is shown only this once.

client_secret.description:
The client's secret; none for a public client. Left out when
changing a provider: it keeps its secret.

issuer.description:
The issuer's URL: its discovery document is at
`<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration`.

label.description: What the sign-in button says, e.g. "Company SSO".

path.description: Its path (`/`, or `/…/`); `/` if not given.

rate.description: Object versions per hour, across the cluster; 0 pauses sweeps.

access_key.description:
Whether it gets an access key (a service's), of a random ID; a person
gets none, and signs in to the console through its link.

boundary.description: Its permissions boundary: a managed policy's ARN.

path.description: Its path (`/`, or `/…/`); `/` if not given.

secret.description:
The access key's secret: at least 8 characters; one is generated if
not given. Implies `access_key`.
At least 8 characters; one is generated if not given.

NewSetting.description:
Sets the rate lifecycle sweeps go at, for the whole cluster.
A cluster setting's new value; `null` unsets it (it's back to its
default, or for `parity-shards`, every node goes by its flag again).

tags.description: The whole tag set (none: no tags).

NewUser.description:
A new user: its access key's ID and secret, if it got one, which is
shown only this once.

NodeCoverage.description:
The copies of committed, checksummed blobs a node holds, and how recently
they were known intact.

oldest_checked.description: When the least recently checked of the others was known intact.

unchecked.description:
Copies never checked (from before scrubbing), or flagged by a read:
checked next.

NodeHolding.description:
The committed blobs a node holds a shard of, and the bytes of those
shards.

shards.description: The shards it holds, which move to other nodes.

oneOf.description: The filesystem of its data dir, if it could tell.
Its KMS, if it has one (see `kms`).

now.description: The node's clock, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

scrub_rate.description: How many bytes per second its scrubber reads; 0 if it's off.

NodeStats.description:
What a node reports about itself, for the console of any node (see
`peer`'s `/stats`).

ObjectInfo.description: Every version of a key (the newest 200).

versions.description: Newest first; empty if there's no such key.

OidcProvider.description:
An OpenID Connect provider people may sign in to the console at (see
`console::oidc`); never its client secret.

has_secret.description: Whether it has a client secret (else it's a public client).

OidcProviders.description: The providers, and the redirect URI to register with them.

redirect_uri.description: `<console URL>/api/oidc/callback`, if this node serves the console.

url.description: Where to send the browser: the provider's sign-in.

coding.description:
Whether blobs are brought to that layout now: it takes as many live
nodes as shards.

data_shards.description:
What blobs larger than `small_size` are erasure-coded into (the
`data-shards` setting, and the parity shards). One data shard: they
aren't.

max_data_shards.description: The most data and parity shards the settings allow.

parity_setting.description:
The `parity-shards` setting, if it's set; else every node goes by its
`--replication-factor`.

PackerTotals.description: What the packer did since the node started.

etag.description: What to complete the upload with.

backed_up.description: Whether it's synced (backed up) by its provider, as it last said.

current.description: Whether this session was signed in with it.

description.description: Its new description; unchanged if not given.

document.description: Its new document (a new default version); unchanged if not given.

PolicyDocument.description: An inline policy: a JSON document in IAM's policy language.

PolicySummary.description: A managed policy: one of Cairn's (AWS's names), or the account's own.

aws.description: Whether it's one of Cairn's (AWS's), which can't be changed.

bounds.description: The account's users whose permissions boundary it is.

users.description: The account's users it's attached to.

tags.description:
All of its tags (keys case-sensitive): those it has of other keys go
(UntagPolicy), the rest are set (TagPolicy).

PolicyVersion.description: One of a managed policy's versions.

default.description: Whether it's the default, which decides.

ProviderButton.description: A provider to sign in at.

Registration.description:
What `navigator.credentials.create()` gave the page (its parts, in
base64url).

ReplicaGroup.description:
The committed blobs of `data_shards` data shards (1: replicated) with
`copies` shards in all, `live` of them on live nodes. A blob is readable
with `data_shards` live shards, and as redundant as the cluster's
replication factor asks with `data_shards` + replication factor − 1.

history.description: The last hour's slots that had requests, oldest first.

ops.description: Since the node started, by operation.

slot_secs.description: How many seconds a slot of `history` covers.

name.description: Its new name (unique in the account regardless of case).

RoleSummary.description: A role, never with its secret.

attached.description: Its attached managed policies (AdministratorAccess, if it's an admin).

boundary.description: Its permissions boundary's ARN, which caps what its policies allow.

oneOf.description:
How it signs in to the console, if it does (a person's); `None`:
it doesn't, and no link for it is out (a service's).

id.description:
Its ID, which never changes or comes back: its name (alias) in the
KMS's auth mount for Cairn.

keys.description: Its access keys, oldest first (never their secrets).

kms_entity_id.description:
Its identity (entity) in the KMS, which key owners grant keys to;
none until Cairn has logged in as it, or without a KMS.

path.description: Its path (`/`, or `/…/`), which its ARN has before its name.

policies.description: The names of its inline policies.

tags.description:
All of its tags: those it has of other keys go (UntagUser), the
rest are set (TagUser).

expose.description: `ExposeHeader`s: the response headers a page may read.

headers.description: `AllowedHeader`s: what a preflight may ask to send.

max_age.description: `MaxAgeSeconds`: how long a browser may keep a preflight's answer.

ScrubTotals.description:
What the scrubber did since the node started: the copies it checked (and
their bytes), how many of them it found damaged or missing, how many of
those it repaired, and how many have data that's intact nowhere, and how
many of its passes failed.

Secret.description: A role's secret, which is shown only this once.

warnings.description:
What's wrong with the cluster's layouts now, if anything: too few
nodes for them, say.

t.description: When the slot starts. The same on every node, so slots add up.

Storage.description:
What's stored where, how well it's replicated, and what the background jobs
still have to do.

key.description: The key it has got to.

Tag.description:
A tag of a bucket, an object version (see `s3::tags`) or a user (whose
keys are unique regardless of case).

UserAccess.description: What a user's policies allow it on a whole bucket.

oneOf.description: How it's encrypted; none if it isn't.

lost_bytes.description: How many of its parts' bytes are intact on no replica.

Versioning.description:
A bucket's versioning state. A bucket starts out unversioned; once enabled,
it only moves between enabled and suspended. Serialized as it's stored.
